stem:
Dhruv opens a window of his warm kitchen. The air pressure inside the kitchen is higher than the air pressure outside, and the open window connects the two regions.

What happens to the air?

options.text: Air flows from the kitchen to the outside, and a larger pressure difference makes the flow faster.
Air flows from the outside into the kitchen, and a larger pressure difference makes the flow faster.
Air flows from the kitchen to the outside, and the flow speed stays the same no matter how large the pressure difference is.
Air flows from the kitchen to the outside even if the window is closed and no path connects the two regions.

build_logic.mx_swap: C mapped to scope_error (difference size ignored); term_substitution not used

teacher.key_rationale: Air flows from higher pressure to lower pressure; a larger difference gives faster flow. Kitchen pressure is higher, so air flows out faster when the difference is larger. B reverses flow direction. C treats difference size as irrelevant to speed. D drops the need for a connecting path.
